newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria police seize a million pirate CDs in raid.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria police seize a million pirate CDs in raid.

text.p: Bulgarian police seized an estimated one million pirate compact discs stored in the garage of a modest Sofia house on Wednesday and arrested three men and a woman they said were distributors.
Zahari Zahariev, police chief of Sofia's first district, told reporters the raid followed a report that the CDs had been delivered earlier on Wednesday by a truck.
A man aged about 25 was arrested leaving the tumbledown house with a bag full of CDs.

Two men and a woman were arrested inside the house, where police found a workshop for packing the discs. "They seem to be some of the organisers of this illegal trade," said one policeman who took part in the raid.
Police said vendors sold the discs for up to $3.
Bulgaria's government, which took office in May, has vowed to crack down on the bootleg trade, in which the Balkan country is thought to rank second only to China.
The international recording industry says Bulgaria's annual production of 15 million pirated CDs, exported to Russia, the Baltic states and western Europe, costs it $100 million a year.
Bulgaria took its first piracy case to court last month but the defendant was acquitted for lack of evidence.
Last week Bulgaria's customs officers bulldozed more than 91,000 pirated compact discs worth some $2 million to display their determination to crack down on illegal production.
